title: What a Democratic Congress Means for Latin America
gist: Former U.S. officials Eric Jacobstein and Emily Mendrala argue that the Democratic midterm sweep of both chambers will bring aggressive oversight of Trump's Latin America policy, from Venezuela oil deals to ICE and CECOT, tariffs and appropriations. They also expect a constrained Trump to grow more aggressive abroad, with Cuba the main flashpoint and Mexico strikes and the Panama Canal as latent risks.

themes.theme: Divided government pushes Trump to act abroad

insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: Divided government changes the odds on legislation, oversight and appropriations for 2027–28.

insights.claim: It is dangerous to assume that Trump will inevitably retreat on Cuba or that a Democratic Congress will check his power there.
insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: Do not price Congress as a constraint on Cuba policy.
insights.quote: Assuming Trump will inevitably retreat—or that a Democratic Congress would serve as a check on his power vis-à-vis Cuba—is dangerous.

insights.claim: Cuba is the clearest place to watch. A domestically constrained Trump may push aggressively for negotiations to force economic and political change there, or use military force.
insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: Cuba confrontation risk affects Caribbean tourism and shipping, and Florida politics.
insights.quote: Constrained domestically, Trump will find a confrontation with the Caribbean island especially attractive.
insights.locator: Cuba is the clearest place to watch.

insights.claim: Military force against Cuba looks less likely in the short term than several months ago, mainly because hostilities with Iran have resumed and are drawing U.S. attention.
insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: U.S. military bandwidth is a constraint. A de-escalation with Iran could raise Cuba risk.
insights.locator: Cuba is the clearest place to watch.

themes.theme: New oversight: Venezuela deals and corruption

insights.claim: Rep. Joaquin Castro, expected to lead the House Western Hemisphere Subcommittee, sought subpoenas in September for records on the administration's Venezuela oil agreement involving Barbados-based North American Blue Energy Partners, and he can now pursue that probe with a majority.
insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: Companies in Trump-era Venezuela oil deals face investigation and headline risk.

insights.claim: With new Democratic leadership on Latin America in both chambers, parties to deals in Venezuela and elsewhere in the Americas should expect scrutiny of beneficiaries and possible corruption, which Hakeem Jeffries has named as the guiding principle of Democratic oversight.
insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: This adds diligence and reputational risk to politically brokered LatAm energy and resource deals.
insights.quote: those involved in deals in Venezuela (and elsewhere in the Americas) should expect scrutiny of beneficiaries and possible corruption

insights.claim: Sen. Chris Coons, the likely next Senate Foreign Relations chair, pressed Secretary of State Marco Rubio over not consulting Congress before Maduro's removal and backed limits on further military operations.
insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: Expect war-powers fights over further Venezuela operations.

insights.claim: Rep. Gregory Meeks, expected to chair House Foreign Affairs, warned in October that Abelardo De La Espriella's electoral intervention put bipartisan U.S. support for Colombia at risk.
insights.speaker: ERIC JACOBSTEIN AND EMILY MENDRALA
insights.so_what: Bipartisan U.S. support for Colombia, including aid and trade goodwill, could become conditional.

insights.claim: Endorsements of Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar by Colombia's De La Espriella, Argentina's Javier Milei and María Corina Machado were shortsighted, because they tied foreign leaders to one U.S. party and complicated ties with Democrats.
